title: Injective approximation with ideal-power torsion cokernel
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, with $R/I\to S/IS$ bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] with prime module $S\otimes_R M$ [def-weil-module-base-change], chart modules $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and comparison and interchange maps the canonical ones for every $M$ (bundled equalities for the modules, heterogeneous equalities for the structural linear maps). All modules lie in universe $\max(u,v,w)$, where $R$ and $S$ lie in universes $u$ and $v$. For every datum $X$ there exist an $R$-module $H$ in that universe and a glueing morphism $\psi:\mathrm{Can}(H)\to X$ such that $\psi'$ is injective, each chart map $\psi_i$ is bijective, and every element $x$ of $Q=X.M'/\operatorname{im}\psi'$, regarded as an $R$-module through $\varphi$, has an integer $n\ge1$ with $I^n x=0$. This conclusion is an approximation; it does not assert that $\psi'$ is surjective.

proof.text: Construct H as ModuleCat.of R (h0 φ f X), the actual submodule of compatible families [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0]. Tensor the prime projection to obtain the S-linear map p(s tensor h)=s h.val.1 [def-weil-module-base-change]. For each chart take the unique bijective extension π_i supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0-localization]. Its source is the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. The prime compatibility holds on (s tensor h)/1 by the prime/chart defining equation of h0, the defining universal-property equation of FormalGlueing.compare in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], and S-linearity of alpha. Tensor induction and localization extensionality prove it everywhere. The overlap compatibility holds on (h/1)/1 by the defining overlap equation and the defining equation of swap in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]; two applications of localization extensionality prove it everywhere. Restriction of the canonical localized chart to R equals the localized R-module by algebraMap_smul. Transport all components along the given bundled module equalities; elimination of those equalities and the heterogeneous structural-map equalities transports both compatibility equations. This gives ψ:Can.obj H → X with bijective charts and ψ.prime(e.symm(1 tensor h))=h.val.1, where e is the given prime-module identification.

For any morphism of glueing data with bijective chart maps, not merely the constructed ψ, extend each chart linear equivalence to scalars S. The prime compatibility equation identifies alpha_target composed with the localized prime map with this extended chart equivalence composed with alpha_source. Both alpha maps are equivalences [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], so the localized prime map is bijective [def-weil-module-base-change]. This avoids using a separate bijectivity theorem for the canonical comparison map.

A prime-kernel element maps to zero in every localization, by injectivity from step 2. For the prime cokernel Q, restrict the quotient map q to R. Its composite with ψ.prime is zero. Functoriality of the localized linear maps [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] makes their localized composite zero as well. Every cokernel element has a representative in X.M prime; surjectivity of the localized prime map from step 2 shows the localization of that representative has zero quotient. Thus each cokernel element also maps to zero in every localization. For an element x in either module, the localization equality criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives, for each i, a power of f_i killing x. Hence I=span(range f) lies in the radical of the annihilator J of the cyclic submodule generated by x. I is finitely generated because Fin t is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power], implemented by Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg, to get I^n ≤ J. Therefore x belongs to Ideal.primaryComponent. For the stated cokernel conclusion increase n to n+1, using containment of ideal powers. This also handles an empty chart family: the generated ideal is zero.

Take y in the prime kernel. Transport its ideal-power torsion from step 3 along the S-linear identification e of Can.obj H prime with S tensor H; restriction of scalars makes this an R-linear identification as well. By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso], using flatness, finite generation of I, and the quotient-map bijectivity hypothesis, write e(y)=1 tensor h for an I-power-torsion h in H. The prime formula from step 1 shows h.val.1=0. If I^n kills h, then (f_i)^n kills h for every i. Projecting this equality into chart i gives an equality killed by the unit algebraMap R R_fi ((f_i)^n). Multiplication by a unit is injective, so every h.val.2 i=0. Subtype and product extensionality give h=0; hence e(y)=0 and y=0. The prime map is injective. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves the unchanged approximation statement.

theorem exists_injective_approximation {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f) :
    ∃ (H : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (ψ : Can.obj H ⟶ X),
      Function.Injective ψ.prime ∧ (∀ i, Function.Bijective (ψ.chart i)) ∧
      ∀ x : restrict φ (ModuleCat.of S (X.M' ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ.prime)),
        ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∀ r ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ^ n, r • x = 0
